chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad said:

Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) mentioned that he ordered the one who asked him about a man who prayed beside a man, so he stood on his left, and he did not know. Then he realized while he was in his prayer how he should act. He said: 'He should move him to his right.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone stands on the left side of the Imam in prayer without knowing it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the procedural etiquette of *saff* (prayer rows) by instructing that a worshipper unaware of their position relative to the Imam should be moved to the right side to maintain proper alignment. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on order and the physical perfection of the congregational formation, ensuring the row remains straight and cohesive even when minor positional errors occur during the prayer itself.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said,

‘Al-Husayn mentioned that heasws ordered the one who asked himasws about a man who prays to the side of a man, so she stand on his left, and he did not know. Then he comes to know while he was during his Salāt how he should be doing it, said: ‘He should transfer to be on his right’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad who has the following:

Al-Husayn has mentioned that he (the Imam), ’Alayhi al-Salam, commanded a man, who was asking him (the Imam) about a man who was performing Salah (prayer) on the side of a man standing on his left. He did not know (that he is to stand on the right side of the Imam) and then he learned in his Salah (prayer) how he is to do. He (the Imam) commanded to turn him to his right.”
